answers.ask: Cel-shading is a render style rather than a setting - should the gallery read as a clean white-cube museum, a cosy home studio, or something else?
answers.answer: Make it a clean white-cube museum rendered in cel-shaded 3D, with the easel prominently placed at the front.

answers.ask: How many finished portraits should the gallery be sized to hold before it has to expand?
answers.answer: Size the initial gallery for 12 finished portraits before it expands.

scene_prompt: Create a cel-shaded 3D game map as a clean white-cube museum gallery sized to display 12 finished portrait images. A prominent 3D easel stands at the front of the gallery holding the most recent portrait, while the remaining portrait display spaces line the surrounding white walls for players to walk up to and inspect.
agent_notes: The painting round is a UI activity with no geometry, so the only thing being laid out is the gallery the player walks around and inspects — that is Entertainment's Indoor Venue, the museum and gallery case. interior-single is the shape because the white-cube gallery is the entire map: the player never steps outside, so there is no exterior to generate and no transition to link, which keeps it on P0 rather than the P3 an enterable building would cost. landmark-focal is the easel at the front holding the most recent portrait, the one piece the room is composed around, and vignette-photo carries the inspection viewpoints in front of each hung work; I dropped social-hub because this reads as a personal gallery rather than a crowd space, and zone-graphics because cel-shading is a render style rather than a detail cluster to isolate. Without a user to ask I sized the room for the twelve portraits the answers gave, arranged so the walls can extend when it expands, and left the colour unlocks entirely to UI.
